starting_principles: Rotational equation of motion for a system: $\vec{\tau}_{\text{net, ext}} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$
Fixed-axis rigid body angular momentum: $L_z = I_z \omega$
Work-energy theorem for rotational kinetic energy: $K = \frac{L^2}{2I}$
assumptions: The system rotates about a specified fixed axis (e.g. $z$-axis).
The net external torque component along this axis is zero: $\tau_{\text{ext}, z} = 0$.
Changes in moment of inertia occur solely through internal mechanisms.

ordered_steps.description: State the fundamental dynamical equation relating external torque to the rate of change of total angular momentum.
ordered_steps.operation: Project the vector equation onto the fixed axis of rotation (taken as the $z$-axis): $\tau_{\text{net, ext}, z} = \frac{dL_z}{dt}$.
assumptions_applied: Axis of rotation is fixed in orientation.

ordered_steps.description: Apply the physical condition of zero net external torque along the rotation axis.
assumptions_applied: System is isolated from external torques about the $z$-axis.

ordered_steps.description: Integrate the rate equation between initial state ($t_i$) and final state ($t_f$).
ordered_steps.operation: Integrate both sides from $t_i$ to $t_f$: $\int_{t_i}^{t_f} \frac{dL_z}{dt} \, dt = 0 \implies L_z(t_f) - L_z(t_i) = 0$.
assumptions_applied: Continuity of angular momentum across the time interval.

ordered_steps.description: Substitute the constitutive relationship for fixed-axis rotation $L_z = I \omega$ at both states.
ordered_steps.operation: Substitute initial state $L_{z, i} = I_i \omega_i$ and final state $L_{z, f} = I_f \omega_f$ into the conservation relation.

ordered_steps.description: Solve for the final angular velocity in terms of the initial state and the ratio of moments of inertia.
Examine the non-conservation of rotational kinetic energy to verify physical work-energy consistency.
ordered_steps.operation: Express kinetic energy ratio using constant $L$: $\frac{K_f}{K_i} = \frac{I_i}{I_f}$. If moment of inertia decreases ($I_f < I_i$), kinetic energy increases: $\Delta K = K_f - K_i = W_{\text{internal}} > 0$.
assumptions_applied: Internal forces perform work during mass redistribution.

applicability_conditions: Net external torque along the axis of rotation must be zero during the entire transition.
Does not require mechanical energy conservation.
Applies to deformable bodies, coupled spinning discs, or systems with internal radial motion.
